commodity_commentary: Commodity markets posted a mixed week as energy reversed sharply while precious and base metals advanced — WTI fell 11.74% on the week to US$80.58/bbl and Brent fell 11.69% to US$83.23/bbl, an unwind of the supply-shock premium that had carried crude above US$100/bbl a month earlier, leaving WTI down 23.56% over the month.32 Precious metals held firm as gold settled at US$4,353.30/oz, up 31.07% year-over-year, and silver at US$70.22/oz, up 93.53% year-over-year — the steepest 52-week percentage advance of any commodity tracked here, against a 52-week low of US$35.70/oz.32 Base metals firmed with copper at US$6.51/lb, near its 52-week high of US$6.58/lb and up 35.59% year-over-year, on sustained Chinese industrial demand after the May NBS Manufacturing PMI printed 50.0.25 Prairie staples were mixed: wheat held at US$586.25/bu (+0.51% on the week, +7.82% year-over-year) while the StatCan canola farm price registered CAD$733.20/t for the May reference, its 52-week high.16 Lumber rose 3.10% to US$631.00/mfbm, the firmest weekly move among forest products.32 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties commodity moves to 551 active Canadian mining projects ($199.9B aggregate) and 91 oil and gas projects ($63.2B).32

commodities.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
commodities.context: WTI crude settled at US$80.58 per barrel, down 11.74% on the week and 23.56% over the month — the decline came as the geopolitical premium that had carried crude above US$100 per barrel a month earlier eased through the week's trade.32 The 52-week range runs US$55.27 to US$112.95 per barrel, and WTI's +10.41% year-over-year reading sits above the one-year average of US$72.33 per barrel.32 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties WTI to 91 active Canadian oil and gas projects ($63.2B aggregate). If WTI holds above US$74-76 per barrel — the Alberta breakeven cluster the engine cites for those projects — the 91 oil and gas projects would maintain netbacks above that threshold, even as April energy exports rose 9.7% m/m to $19.88B.14

commodities.name: Crude Oil (Brent)
commodities.context: Brent crude settled at US$83.23 per barrel, down 11.69% on the week and 22.98% over the month — the global benchmark tracked WTI lower as the same supply-premium unwind played through, against a 52-week high of US$118.35 per barrel and a one-year average of US$76.58 per barrel.32

commodities.name: Natural Gas
commodities.context: Natural gas settled at US$3.08 per million British thermal units, down 1.57% on the week and 1.44% over the month — the year-over-year reading of -14.11% reflects the unwind of 2025 winter pricing, with the 52-week range running US$2.70 to US$6.80 per MMBtu and the one-year average at US$3.52 per MMBtu.32 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties Henry Hub to Canadian LNG export economics, with utilities-sector capital spend tracked across 795 active projects ($599.3B aggregate) priced in part against gas-input differentials.32

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.context: Gold settled at US$4,353.30 per ounce, up 0.05% on the week and 31.07% year-over-year — the metal eased 4.78% over the month from its 52-week high of US$5,318.40 per ounce, holding above a one-year average of US$4,076.56 per ounce.32 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties gold to the database's 551 active Canadian mining projects ($199.9B aggregate). If gold holds above US$4,000 per ounce through the third quarter, those mining projects would retain the cost coverage cited in their public filings, with the metal's +31.07% annual move marking its largest year-over-year gain in the 52-week window.32

commodities.name: Silver
commodities.context: Silver settled at US$70.22 per ounce, up 2.77% on the week and 93.53% year-over-year — the annual move is the steepest 52-week percentage advance of any tracked commodity, against a 52-week high of US$115.08 per ounce and a 52-week low of US$35.70 per ounce.32

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.context: Copper settled at US$6.51 per pound, up 2.12% on the week and 35.59% year-over-year — the advance came as the May NBS Manufacturing PMI reading of 50.0 and the equipment-manufacturing sub-index at 52.1 reflected sustained Chinese industrial demand, with the print sitting at its highest in the 52-week window against a range of US$4.33 to US$6.58 per pound.25

commodities.name: Nickel
commodities.context: Nickel registered a monthly-average reading of US$18,879.23 per tonne, up 10.56% over the month and 25.84% year-over-year — the FRED monthly series is the only nickel signal in pipeline data, with no spot quote computable, and the latest print sits at its 52-week high.32 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties nickel to the Ontario and Quebec battery-materials supply chain feeding the database's 551 active mining projects ($199.9B aggregate).32

commodities.name: Wheat
commodities.context: Wheat settled at US$586.25 per bushel, up 0.51% on the week and 7.82% year-over-year — the contract eased 8.00% over the month, with the 52-week high of US$668.25 and low of US$495.00 bracketing a one-year average of US$549.95 per bushel.32

commodities.name: Canola
commodities.context: Canola registered a StatCan farm-price reading of CAD$733.20 per tonne for the May 2026 reference — the 32-10-0077 monthly farm-price series, not a futures or spot quote, stands up 8.98% over the month and 11.92% year-over-year at its 52-week high, feeding Prairie oilseed producer revenue.16
commodities.note: StatCan 32-10-0077 farm price — monthly. Labelled farm price (monthly), never futures or spot.

commodities.name: Potash (Nutrien)
commodities.context: The Nutrien share-price proxy closed at CAD$92.68, down 1.43% on the week and up 8.50% year-over-year — the NTR.TO equity price stands in for the Saskatchewan potash sector, not a US$-denominated spot quote, easing 5.86% over the month against a 52-week range of CAD$75.58 to CAD$114.41.32
commodities.note: Nutrien (NTR.TO) share-price proxy, CAD$ — NOT a US$ potash spot price.

commodities.name: Lumber
commodities.context: Lumber settled at US$631.00 per thousand board feet, up 3.10% on the week and 6.95% over the month — the advance came as US housing starts for May were released, a lumber-demand signal for Canadian forestry exporters, with the year-over-year reading of +0.72% in line with the one-year average of US$585.46 against a 52-week high of US$695.50.35 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties lumber to Canadian construction-input demand: Canadian housing starts rose to 279,317 SAAR in May (+6.9% m/m), and the database tracks 272 active residential projects ($41.6B aggregate) drawing on framing lumber.17
